To start the game in the 4x4x4 Twist Four cube, controlling the center of the board is a strong foundational strategy, similar to traditional Connect Four or Tic-Tac-Toe variants. Dropping a piece into the center-front shaft (B2) gives us a solid base from which to build multi-directional winning lines.

MOVE: drop B2

Since we are on Turn 3 and only two pieces have been dropped (X at B2, O at D3, both on layer 1), the tactical landscape is very open. Building toward potential 3D diagonals or lines in layer 1 is a good strategy. Let's drop another piece near the center to increase our control and options.

MOVE: drop C2

To continue building our position while blocking potential threats and setting up our own winning lines in this 3D Connect Four variant, let's control the center. Column B, row 3 is currently empty, and dropping a piece there places it at the bottom of the B3 shaft on layer 1, adding to our control of the board.

MOVE: drop B3

We currently have a strong cluster of X pieces in the center of layer L1 (B2, C2, B3) and need to build a winning line. Let's drop another piece into shaft B to strengthen our column/shaft control and set up potential alignment threats.

MOVE: drop B1

To create an immediate threat or build toward a winning line, dropping a piece in shaft B to build up the stack is a strong approach. Let's place an X on B to reinforce the column and create alignment opportunities.
